chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from al-A'la ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

When a man hears a testimony but was not called to witness upon it, he is free to choose — if he so desires, he may testify, and if he so desires, he may remain silent — except when he knows [the matter involves wrongdoing] from the oppressor, then he must testify, and it is not permissible for him except that he testifies.

key_terms.الشَّهَادَةُ: testimony/witnessing — the formal act of giving evidence before a judicial authority in Islamic law
key_terms.الظَّالِم: the oppressor/wrongdoer — one who commits injustice; key term triggering the mandatory testimony exception
key_terms.الْخِيَار: option/free choice — the legal status of having discretion to act or abstain
key_terms.يَحِلّ: is permissible — from the root relating to what is halal; here used in negative form to indicate prohibition

ai.seo_question: According to Imam al-Baqir, is a person who accidentally hears a testimony obligated to testify in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Baqir (AS) addresses an important jurisprudential question: the obligation of a person who inadvertently overhears a testimony without being formally designated as a witness. The Imam establishes a general rule of discretion — such a person is not compelled to come forward — but carves out a crucial exception: when the matter involves an oppressor and the person's knowledge could prevent injustice, testifying becomes obligatory. This ruling reflects the broader Islamic legal principle that preventing oppression takes precedence over individual choice, grounding the duty to testify in the moral imperative to oppose injustice.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Al A’ala Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘When the man hears the testimony but did not witness upon it, so he is with the choice, if he so desires to he testifies, and if he so desires to he remains silent, except when he knows from the oppressor, so let him testify, and there is no way out for him except that he testifies’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from al-‘Ala’ ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has narrated the following: “Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

If a man hears a testimony but has not witnessed it, he has the choice to testify or remain silent, unless he knows that a rightful party suffers injustice, in which case it is not lawful to remain silent.’”
